get.summary: Export a cluster's recorded operations for meshctl kube audit-check
get.description: Requires audit.export in the Workspace or the Network. The body is the meshtransit-kube-operations/v1 file meshctl reads, not wrapped in data: the header, the records from records_from to records_to (5 minutes past each side), then complete: true. A range of at most a day and 200000 records (422 range_too_large), ending at least 6 minutes ago so its records (5 minutes past to) have settled (422 range_not_settled; to defaults to 6 minutes ago); a cluster without a signing trust has no gateway namespace (409); one export a Workspace runs at a time on a replica (429). A failure while streaming writes a token no JSON reader accepts and cuts the connection: a cut file never reads as whole.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start (inclusive); default: a day before to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End (exclusive); default: now. At most a day after from.

200.description: The file

status.description: 0 without an outcome within a day

put.description: Requires kubernetes_cluster.manage and audit.export. If-Match is the version read ("0" before any). Lists are sorted and made distinct; the same lists change nothing (changed: false). An administrator types them as the gateway chart's values say: the gateway never sets them.

A page reads at most 50000 operations whatever the filters keep: scan_truncated says it stopped early, and next_page_token continues from there. A malformed query or a page_token of another cluster answers 404.

parameters.description: Start (inclusive); default: a day before to.

post.summary: Ask the CA worker to retire one of a cluster's certificate authorities
post.description: Requires kubernetes_cluster.approve. Core records the request; the CA worker retires the CA (a root with its intermediates) within its next pass and marks the request done, or refuses it: expired after an hour, changed when the CA moved past ca_version, guard while a database restore is suspected (but for compromise), gone when the CA was already retired. A waiting request for the same CA and reason is returned unchanged (200, created false); another reason waiting is 409 retire_request_pending. At most 5 requests a person an hour (429 retire_rate_limited). change_ref and note hold no secrets or personal data.

200.description: A request for the same CA and reason already waits

can_change_ratchet.description: The caller holds kubernetes_cluster.approve, so may suspend or resume the replicas' ratchets; a hint, the action checks again.

post.summary: Let a replica's sessions run without a pod token for a while
post.description: Requires kubernetes_cluster.approve. For a replica that proved a pod token before (409 replica_not_ratcheted otherwise): its sessions may run without a token until duration_seconds (5 minutes to a day) from now, replacing a suspension it had; a token proven meanwhile ends the suspension. Sessions let through end when it does. A copy of the replica's Secret connects too while it holds: suspend only to fix a gateway that lost its token, with a change reference. After 10 suspensions and resumes by a person within an hour, a suspension is refused (429 ratchet_change_rate_limited); a resume never is. reason and change_ref hold no secrets or personal data.

change_ref.description: A ticket or incident reference; printable, no line breaks.

200.description: The ratchet is suspended until ratchet_suspended_until

post.summary: End a replica's ratchet suspension now
post.description: Requires kubernetes_cluster.approve. Sessions without a token that the suspension let through end within 30 seconds. With nothing suspended nothing changes (changed false). Never rate limited; counts toward the 10 changes after which a person's suspensions are refused for the hour.

200.description: The ratchet holds again

post.description: Requires enrollment_credential.issue (the owner, admin or it_admin). Creates a key that enrolls exactly one Device into the Network. The key is usable for key_lifetime_seconds (24 hours by default); the Device it enrolls lives device_lifetime_seconds from registration, or never expires. The Device belongs to the caller. A Network has at most 100 usable keys. Recorded as enrollment_key.created. post.description: Requires kubernetes_cluster.approve. The code is what the replica prints in its log (enroll code: XXXXX-XXXXX); case, spaces and hyphens do not matter. A code that is not ten base32 characters is invalid_request and not counted. A wrong code answers join_code_wrong (422) with the attempts left; the fifth cancels the request (replica_request_cancelled, 409). A matching code consumes one use of the key, reserves an ordinal and the name <cluster>-<ordinal>, and gives the replica 15 minutes to complete; a key no longer usable cancels the request instead (join_key_not_usable, 409). Recorded as kubernetes_replica_request.approved, .code_failed or .cancelled.

destination_prefixes.description: The prefixes a Site rule grants; present only when selector_kind is site.

kubernetes_groups.description: The Kubernetes groups a rule to a cluster grants, sorted; absent when it grants none, as for a rule published before Kubernetes groups.

KubernetesAccessProfileRule.description: One rule as RBAC's PolicyRule (rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1): a resource rule (apiGroups, resources, maybe resourceNames) or, in the cluster part only, a path rule (nonResourceURLs).

id.description: A UUIDv7 the client makes for a new profile and keeps across edits; unique to the Network.

name.description: Unique in the release; part of the content a rule pins.

description.description: Shown only; not part of what the release grants.

namespaced.description: Applied in the namespaces of the rule that uses the profile.

cluster.description: Cluster-scoped resources and paths; only for a rule that turns the cluster part on.

KubernetesAccessProfile.description: A Kubernetes access profile (K2 §5.1): what a rule to a cluster may do within the groups it grants. It only narrows: the cluster's RBAC of each group stays the ceiling. At least one rule; at most 16 KiB normalized.

full.description: The rule grants its groups in full; nothing else may be set.

namespaces.description: ["*"] alone for every namespace, or 1 to 64 DNS labels.

report_until.description: With mode report only: when the rule starts to enforce, after now and at most 14 days ahead.

KubernetesAccess.description: With destination_kubernetes_cluster_id only: how the rule grants its Kubernetes groups, {"full": true} or through a profile. Absent or null keeps what the rule has in the active release, whatever kubernetes_groups says; {} is refused. A rule with a profile that moves to another source or cluster must say its access again (kubernetes_access_required).

approval_evidence_id.description: Optional for direct publication by an authorized policy publisher. When supplied, immutable approval evidence is freshly validated and consumed; invalid evidence is never ignored.

kubernetes_profiles.description: Every Kubernetes access profile of the release (K2), the whole set. Absent or null keeps the profiles of the active release; an empty list removes them all. A profile a kept or named rule applies must be in the set.

CompiledPolicyRule.description: Exactly one source (a Device, Device Group, Identity Group or tag) and one destination. A selector source takes a Device, Device Group or tag destination only, an Identity Group is a source only, and a Device-to-Device rule names no selector. A Site or Exit Pool destination takes any source.

source_identity_group_id.description: A Workspace Identity Group: the untagged Devices its active members own in the Network.

source_device_tag_id.description: Every Device of the Network that carries the tag.

destination_device_tag_id.description: Every Device of the Network that carries the tag.

destination_site_id.description: A Site of the Network: the rule grants routes into it (needs subnet routes on the deployment).

destination_prefixes.description: With destination_site_id only: the part of the Site the rule grants, as canonical CIDRs inside the Site; absent or empty for the whole Site.

destination_exit_pool_id.description: An Exit Pool of the Network: the rule grants the Internet through its exit nodes, on the rule's protocol and ports. Takes no destination_prefixes.

destination_kubernetes_cluster_id.description: A Kubernetes cluster of the Network: the rule grants kubectl to every replica of the cluster, now and later. TCP port 443 only; the source is a Device, Device Group, Identity Group or tag.

kubernetes_groups.description: With destination_kubernetes_cluster_id only: the Kubernetes groups the rule grants, names of groups declared in the cluster gateway's Helm values. Absent keeps the groups the rule has in the active release, while it comes from the same source to the same cluster; an empty list is refused; a new or retargeted rule to a cluster needs at least one.

kubernetes_profiles.description: Every Kubernetes access profile of the release (K2), the whole set. Absent or null keeps the profiles of the active release; an empty list removes them all. A profile a kept or named rule applies must be in the set.

Every Kubernetes access profile of the release (K2), the whole set. Absent or null keeps the profiles of the active release; an empty list removes them all. A profile a kept or named rule applies must be in the set.

PolicyPeerEstimate.description: How many peers the proposed policy puts in each Device's map, counted per rule side without expanding group rules. Core sends at most limit peers per map (a prioritized subset beyond it).

max_peers.description: Largest number of peers one Device would see; an upper bound unless exact

exact.description: False when group rules make the counts upper bounds

guardrail_findings.description: Guardrails the proposed paths to Imported Resources break, as publication applies them: the publishing Workspace's (named) and, only where it blocks, the provider Workspace's (never named). blocks is true for an enforced guardrail on a path the active release does not already open; publication refuses such a draft. Blocking findings come first; guardrail_finding_count is the total.

guardrail.description: The publishing Workspace's guardrail; null for the provider's.

PolicySimulationImportedIntentChanges.description: Present exactly when either compiled candidate is format 4. Reports Consumer-local intent and bilateral provenance, not effective cross-scope packet access.

PolicySimulationSiteAccessChanges.description: Present when the current policy or the proposal has a rule to a Site. Lists, per source Device, the access to part of a Site the proposal adds and removes; at most 256 entries each, the counts carry the totals.

prefixes.description: The part of the Site the rule grants; empty for all of it.

destination_kubernetes_cluster_id.description: A Kubernetes cluster (the caller must also read it, network.read): explained through its active replica of the lowest ordinal, named in target.device_id. 404 kubernetes_cluster_not_found when unknown, 409 kubernetes_cluster_no_active_replica when it has no active replica.

destination_address.description: A unicast address: the explanation's target is the Site that holds it or, for an Internet address no Site holds, the Exit Pool it is reached through.

deny_reason.description: Present exactly when decision is deny. Classified in a fixed order: policy, source, share, target, then default deny.

ExplainedPolicyContext.description: Participants of the caller's Network and, for a shared target, the contract facts the consumer already sees. Provider Devices, addresses and Resources are never included.

ExplainedPolicyParticipantState.description: active is usable now; inactive exists but is inactive, deleted, key-expired or ended; missing does not exist in the Network.

nodes.description: Exactly the participants the page's paths connect.

matching_paths.description: Every edge matching the filters in this revision, across all pages.

AccessGraphNode.description: A site or exit_pool node's name is null unless the caller may also read routes.

share.description: The Trust Contract of a shared-in Device; null for other kinds.

state.description: Effective at evaluation time: an activating or active contract past its expiry is expired.

expires_at.description: Null when the share never expires.

access_name.description: Consumer DNS name; a derived name is presented under the deployment's DNS suffix (…shared.<suffix>).

kubernetes_cluster_id.description: The Kubernetes cluster asked about; device_id is then the replica the answer came through.

site_id.description: The Site that holds address; absent when no Site does.

exit_pool_id.description: The Exit Pool an Internet address no Site holds is reached through: the first pool by identity whose active rules grant the Internet to the source Device. Absent when no rule does.

destination_site_id.description: The Site of a path through a rule to a Site; projection_id then names the compiled route rule.

destination_exit_pool_id.description: The Exit Pool of a path through a rule to the Internet; projection_id then names the compiled exit rule.

destination_prefixes.description: The prefixes of the Site the rule grants.

source_device_group_id.description: The source Device Group, when the path comes from a group rule.

destination_device_group_id.description: The destination Device Group, when the path comes from a group rule.

destination_kubernetes_cluster_id.description: The destination Kubernetes cluster, when the path comes from a rule to a cluster; destination_device_id is then one of its replicas and destination_device_group_id is absent.

kubernetes_groups.description: The Kubernetes groups the rule to the cluster grants. Absent when the caller may not read the Network's policy rules, or when the rule grants none (published before Kubernetes groups).

source_identity_group_id.description: The source Identity Group, when the path comes from an Identity Group rule.

source_device_tag_id.description: The source tag, when the path comes from a tag rule.

destination_device_tag_id.description: The destination tag, when the path comes from a tag rule.

expires_at.description: Share grant deadline. Omit when never_expires is true.

never_expires.description: Same-Workspace share remains valid until revoked; cannot be combined with expires_at.

access_label.description: First label of the consumer DNS name <label>.<provider Workspace code>.<provider Network code>.shared.mesh. Canonicalized to lower case; all-digit labels are rejected. Omit to derive it from the shared Resource name. Frozen after creation; within the provider Network a live label names one Resource.

items.description: A fully qualified name, such as app.corp.com; Unicode labels are converted to A-labels

service_names.description: Names the consumer may give the shared Resource, such as the real names its web app serves (DNS design D3). Each is only a suggestion: it resolves nowhere until the consumer approves it when accepting the offer, which makes it a DNS name of the consumer Network that answers the share's alias. Each must be what a DNS zone's domain may be (no special-use name, no public suffix, nothing overlapping the mesh names or covering a name MeshTransit must reach); a refused name answers its DNS zone error with operation_index. Requires MESHTRANSIT_DNS_ZONES_ENABLED.

access_name.description: Forbidden for reject or revoke. On accept of a labeled offer it may be omitted and, when present, must equal the offer access_name; an unlabeled offer requires it. Canonical lower-case consumer-local DNS name; a name ending in .shared.<DNS suffix> is the same name as the offer presents it.

name.description: A name the offer suggests, as the offer shows it

service_names.description: On accept, an answer to each service name the offer suggests, exactly once (dns_service_name_decision_missing otherwise). approve makes the name a DNS name of the consumer Network, in the longest zone that covers it or in a zone of its own whose other names go to each Device's own DNS; it needs dns.manage. A name that cannot be made fails the whole accept with its DNS error and operation_index, the name's place here.

AcceptShareOfferRequest.description: Acceptance-specific request: the imported display name is required. The access name is derived from the provider label and may be omitted; an unlabeled offer still requires it. Reject and revoke continue to use DecideShareOfferRequest and forbid both fields.

trust_contract.description: The Trust Contract this offer was accepted into, as both sides see it.

access_label.description: Frozen provider label; absent for offers created before labels.

access_name.description: Consumer DNS name acceptance reserves; present exactly when access_label is. Derived names are presented under the deployment's DNS suffix: <label>.<workspace code>.<network code>.shared.<suffix> (default suffix mesh.internal).

public.description: The name is on the Internet

service_names.description: The service names the provider suggests, in order; shown when the offer is created or read

expires_at.description: Offer decision deadline, at most seven days after creation.

share_expires_at.description: Share grant deadline after acceptance; 2200-01-01T00:00:00Z represents until revoked.

consumer_network_revision.description: The consumer Network revision the acceptance committed; DNS service names created with it advance the revision further, so wait for maps by a later read, not by this value.

access_name.description: Consumer DNS name; a derived name is presented under the deployment's DNS suffix (…shared.<suffix>).
Consumer DNS name; a derived name is presented under the deployment's DNS suffix (…shared.<suffix>).

remaining_attempts.description: With code join_code_wrong: wrong codes the replica request still accepts before it is cancelled

peer_estimate.description: With code simulation_too_large: the peer counts, which need no Device-by-Device expansion

guardrail_findings.description: With code guardrail_violation: the acting Workspace's enforced guardrails that blocked the change. Code counterpart_guardrail_violation (the other Workspace of a share blocks it) carries none

jwks_rule.description: With code signing_keys_invalid: the rule the pasted JWKS broke

public.description: The name is on the Internet

version.description: 0 while the suggestions are still the offer's

running.description: The contract still runs: the provider may change the suggestions and the consumer use them

dns_names.description: Consumer only: the DNS names of this Network that point at the share, by name

name.description: A current suggestion, as the read shows it

Unauthenticated.description: Missing, malformed, expired, revoked, or stale Account Session.

Forbidden.description: The authenticated principal lacks current exact-scope authority.

InternalFailure.description: Authoritative evidence failed closed because it was internally inconsistent.

NotFound.description: The target is unavailable in the authorized scope.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The resource exists but does not accept this request method.

Conflict.description: Idempotency intent conflict or incompatible terminal state.

Gone.description: The pending protected-change confirmation window expired.

PreconditionFailed.description: The strong mutation version or revision precondition is stale.

UnprocessableEntity.description: The bounded impact set exceeds this API contract.

RateLimited.description: The source or authenticated Account Session exhausted its distributed request budget.

Unavailable.description: Authoritative dependencies, distributed request admission, or bounded process capacity are unavailable.

Timeout.description: The bounded server-side operation deadline expired.
